title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
oneLinerQuestion: Implement a trie supporting insert, search, and startsWith methods.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Implement Trie (Prefix Tree) problem asks us to design an efficient tree data structure for storing strings that supports insert, search, and startsWith operations in O(L) time, where L is the length of the string. A standard hash set can search full strings in O(L) on average, but prefix matching (startsWith) degrades to O(N * L) where N is the total number of words. A Trie solves this by sharing common prefixes among strings. Each node represents a single character branch point containing a mapping to subsequent children nodes and a boolean flag `isWord` (or `isEnd`) indicating whether a complete word terminates at that node.

- Step 1: TrieNode Blueprint Definition — We define a `TrieNode` class comprising two properties: `children`, which is an object/hash map (or fixed-size array of size 26 for lowercase English letters) mapping a character to its child `TrieNode`, and a boolean flag `isWord = false` designating if this node marks the end of a valid word.

- Step 2: Trie Class Constructor — In the `Trie` class constructor, we initialize an empty root node: `this.root = new TrieNode()`. The root node itself does not hold a character; it serves as the universal entry point for all words.

- Step 3: Implementing insert(word) — We initialize a pointer `curr = this.root`. We iterate over each character `char` in `word`: if `!curr.children[char]`, we instantiate a new node `curr.children[char] = new TrieNode()`. We then advance `curr = curr.children[char]`. Once all characters are placed, we mark the terminal node as a complete word: `curr.isWord = true`.

- Step 4: Implementing search(word) — We start at `curr = this.root` and traverse character by character. For each `char` in `word`, if `!curr.children[char]`, the prefix path does not exist, so we immediately return `false`. Otherwise, advance `curr = curr.children[char]`. After traversing all characters, we return `curr.isWord`, ensuring the sequence represents a completed word rather than just an unfinished prefix.

- Step 5: Implementing startsWith(prefix) — We traverse identically to search, starting at `curr = this.root` across each character of `prefix`. If at any point `!curr.children[char]`, no word with this prefix exists, returning `false`. If the entire prefix path exists in the Trie, we return `true` regardless of whether `curr.isWord` is true or false.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(L) for each operation (insert, search, startsWith), where L is the length of the input word or prefix, as each character is processed via an O(1) hash map or array lookup. Space Complexity: O(N * L) auxiliary space in the worst case to store up to N words of average length L, though shared prefixes significantly reduce the total node count in practice.
pseudoCode:
CLASS Trie:
    CONSTRUCTOR(): root = NEW TrieNode()
    FUNCTION insert(word):
        curr = root
        FOR c IN word DO:
            IF c NOT IN curr.children THEN curr.children[c] = NEW TrieNode()
            curr = curr.children[c]
        END FOR
        curr.isWord = True
    FUNCTION search(word):
        node = findNode(word)
        RETURN node IS NOT NULL AND node.isWord
    FUNCTION startsWith(prefix):
        RETURN findNode(prefix) IS NOT NULL
END CLASS
